items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: I cut some tracks at one point with Richard Davis and Tony Williams. We did it as a trio.

ctx.x: Yeah, speaking of critical, have you been in a situation where you really felt you had to tell the supporting musicians that for instance they’re overplaying, let’s keep it basic? I guess I’m thinking of bass players and drummers especially.

Well yes and no. I mean I was very lucky, I got to play with Blue Mitchell. I got to play with great musicians. And even, I mean I cut some tracks at one point with Richard Davis and Tony Williams. We did it as a trio. And I was at one point talking to Tony about what I was hearing. And in the back of my head it’s you can’t tell Tony Williams, who do you think you are? But it’s defused when you’re talking about the music. So it’s not a problem. But I have had the experience for example of working with, see as you…

late ‘60s, early ‘70s, jazz was dead in the water. There were no gigs, there was nothing going on. So you either got involved in pop music or you didn’t, you didn’t work a lot. And I was working as a producer at one point for the CBS Columbia Records arm in England. And they assigned this band to me as a producer, and go produce this band. And after four weeks I went back to the company and say I quit. I said I quit. There’s not a record in these people. You know we’re sitting here in this room and they want me…
